identification: Minimal OOXML MHTML/OLE linked-object test fixture
evidence: Byte-identical to the preexisting repository regression fixture; four stored, readable XML parts only, with no ZIP comment, appended payload, macros or embedded executable.
Package root relationship selects word/document.xml. Its OLEObject r:id=rId7 resolves to the sole external oleObject relationship in word/_rels/document.xml.rels.

Type=Link, UpdateMode=OnCall and ProgID=Test.ProgID. Target is mhtml:https://example.invalid/load/abc!x-usc:https://example.invalid/load/abc. No obfuscation or additional execution path exists in the package.

A protocol-handler relationship establishes a possible remote content load, not remote executable content or exploitative ActiveX. The reserved .invalid destination and placeholder ProgID support inert test construction.

OnCall is not evidence of benignity by itself: the independent attack document also uses OnCall. Office version, policy, host COM registration, endpoint overrides and deployment provenance are unavailable. No invented runtime success or failure is required for this judgment.

remaining_disagreements: Engine-emitted objectives/execution/interpreter::template-injection is a notable generic external-reference observation. Its name and T1221 mapping overstate an OLE link; YAML cannot rename this built-in finding. This is an engine correction, not grounds for another YAML shadow or suppressor.
The inert fixture retains raw ML probability 0.9827852 although both model classes are 0 after correction (previously probability 0.99921477, classes 1). Sensitive operating points can still flag it.

Independent attack document changes from document-model class 1 to both classes 0, probability 0.9996011 -> 0.98106295, risk 237 -> 41. This is a classifier coverage gap with the known hostile parent context; the suspicious relationship signal remains accurate.
The full hostile HTML parent keeps four hostile traits, risk 244, and unchanged probability 0.994933 with model classes 0 before and after; its model-only miss predates this change.

Atomscan embeds an older engine and first failed on unrelated security-hold policy admission. Before/after scans used CLEAVE_VALIDATE=0 against the real checkout; full validation uses the newer local release engine. Model bundle also warns that v18 features omit v19 additions.
OOXML analysis is consolidated into the container report, with no separate XML-member reports. Every original member was inspected and is inventoried above.

Full-validation analysis exposes a stronger version of the same built-in bug: ordinary-https-ole.docx (Test.ProgID, https://example.invalid/workbook.xlsx) is emitted as Hostile template-injection and scores 147. The new YAML MHTML/OLE rule correctly does not match. Retain this negative control outside the global benign fixture corpus rather than relabeling it malicious or allowing the false conviction. No YAML alias or suppression can correct the built-in output.
